# Agentic AI and outbreak modelling

## What I mean by an agent

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- A language model with tools. It reads files, writes code, runs it, and
  loops until a check passes
- Then it opens a pull request, a proposed change to the code that a
  person reviews before it is merged
- I write the task and what counts as right. I read what comes back
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-agent-1.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A brick box on the left, you, the task and what counts as right,
sends a prompt into a loop of four boxes, read the files and the docs,
write or change code, run it, check passed. No returns to the top. Yes
leads to a pull request and a brick box, you, read it, merge or send
back."}
:::
::::

## How I work now

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- I was travelling for summer schools, teaching and workshops, so made
  a very focused go of working through agents
- All code I have produced in the last six months has been agent
  written, pushed from a bot account, a second GitHub login
- Agents write the tasks, from a spec or from a conversation with me
- Review at different levels. Sometimes all the code, sometimes only the
  outcome. A little like working with students
:::

## Agents in the Bundibugyo model: the data

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- The situation reports are French PDFs. Agents read every stream from
  them except confirmed cases and deaths. Those two are cross-checked
  against the INRB-UMIE transcription
- Recent reports get two blind reads. The script exits on an
  undocumented disagreement
- The onset curve exists only as a picture. A digitiser recovers counts
  from pixel colour and axis tick geometry
- Onsets also move between reports because reporting is late. That is a
  nowcasting problem, and it is in the model
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-bvd-sitrep087-page3.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Page 3 of INSP situation report 87, in French. A table of alerts
by province, a bar chart of confirmed cases by date of symptom onset
over 21 days, and a map of cases by health zone."}

::: {.attribution}
INSP SitRep 087, 9 August 2026, page 3,
[insp.cd](https://insp.cd/ebola-17eme-epidemie/)
· `data/README.md` and `scripts/README.md` in [BVDOutbreakSize][bvd-repo],
read 12 September 2026; the onset reporting triangle fit merged
27 July 2026
:::
:::
::::

## Agents in the Bundibugyo model: the model

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Model development through issues and pull requests. 333 of 425 pull
  requests from the bot account
- Performance work by agents, reviewed by agents. 19 perf commits, all
  from bot identities. One review found nothing worth shipping. One
  halved the gradient cost with the log density bit-identical
- Two versions of the model kept in step. The McCabe et al. analogues
  and the joint model share submodels. Every release refits the
  analogues against the published estimates
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-agent-2.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The agent loop again, now fed by a box where agents write the
tasks from a spec or a conversation, with review agents sending findings
back into the loop, me reading all the code or only the outcome, and a
merge that refits in CI and sends new tasks back to the top."}

::: {.attribution}
[BVDOutbreakSize][bvd-repo]: pull request counts from the GitHub search
API, 11 September 2026 · `git log --grep perf`, issue #444, pull request
#656 · analysis page sections *Top-level composers* and *Imperial report
sense check*, read 12 September 2026
:::
:::
::::

## What agents made possible

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Going wide. One posterior over the situation report streams, the
  Uganda exports and a genomic bound
- Checks on every rebuild. Predictive checks per stream, forecasts
  scored against later data, the McCabe replication
- That much debugging would not have happened by hand. The workflow is
  what kept it reviewable
- Agents did not choose the model or judge the ascertainment
  assumption. Infrastructure and review were still needed
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-workflow-agents.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The six-step workflow, question, data, model, fit, check and
report, with a tag over each. People over question; agents read and
digitise over data; people choose, agents write over model; agents,
every push over fit; agents run, people judge over check; agents draft,
people sign over report."}

::: {.attribution}
README and `docs/src/news.md` of [BVDOutbreakSize][bvd-repo], read
12 September 2026 · [A workflow for infectious disease modelling][wf],
Abbott et al.
:::
:::
::::

## Digitising from figures, and what went wrong

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- SitRep 081. JPEG compression left the axis ticks one pixel tall. About
  10 of 19 ticks found, and a total 54% under the printed one
- SitRep 087. The y-axis grid moved from steps of 20 to 25. Caught only
  because it broke the reporting-triangle invariant on dates that should
  have been stable
- SitRep 098. A losslessly encoded image read about 7% high against
  both neighbours and was excluded
- Every fix must reproduce every previously committed block unchanged
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-bvd-onset-raster-087.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The raster image embedded in situation report 87. Confirmed
cases by date of symptom onset from April to August 2026 as stacked bars,
alive in light blue and died in red, a dashed red line at the first
positive laboratory result, a y-axis in steps of 25 and a shaded band on
the right for potentially incomplete data."}

::: {.attribution}
The embedded image from INSP SitRep 087, 9 August 2026, page 3
· `data/README.md` in [BVDOutbreakSize][bvd-repo], notes for SitReps
081, 087 and 098, and issue #594
:::
:::

## Agents that search over models

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- For the Bundibugyo model this was ad hoc. Agents proposed patches to
  the model as issues, one branch each, and every release scored the
  forecast against later data
- The systematic version is a tree. An agent proposes candidate models,
  one loop each, fit and score, keep the best, branch again
- The score is the thing that can be gamed
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-agent-3.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A tree. The current model at the root branches into three
candidates, add a stream, change the delay prior, and split Rt by
province. Two are kept and branch again into three each; one child of
each is kept in teal and the rest are grey, and the kept branches meet
at a box reading keep the best, branch again."}

::: {.attribution}
Open `patch model` issues from `seabbs-bot` in [BVDOutbreakSize][bvd-repo],
11 September 2026, and the forecast scoring in `src/scoring.jl`
:::
:::
::::

## Google SAI in the CDC hubs

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- Martinson et al. 2026. An LLM-guided tree search that writes
  forecasting code. An ensemble of the survivors went to the FluSight,
  COVID-19 and RSV hubs
- Prospective, 2025/26 season. It matched or beat the CDC hub ensembles
  and topped the leader board for all three
- Bracher and Funk 2026. The earlier retrospective gain of 11% came
  from data revisions leaking into the evaluation
- Less epidemiological knowledge than the hand-built models. The hubs,
  the data and the review were still built by people
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/keynote-sai-arxiv.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The arXiv abstract page for Prospective multi-pathogen disease
forecasting using autonomous LLM-guided tree search, by Martinson,
Brenner, Plomecka, Williams, Reich and Shamsi, submitted 15 May 2026."}

::: {.attribution}
Martinson, Brenner, Plomecka, Williams, Reich and Shamsi 2026,
[arXiv:2605.16238](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16238), read 12 September
2026 · Bracher and Funk 2026,
[arXiv:2608.05883](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.05883)
· team folders `Google_SAI-*` in the three hubs on GitHub
:::
:::

## Who gets to do this

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; margin-top: 0.4em; margin-bottom: 0.9em;"}
The people modelling outbreaks where outbreaks happen are the least
likely to have paid access. I do not have a defence for this. I am part
of the problem.
:::

- A Claude Max subscription. £200 a month, from my own pocket. My
  institution does not cover it, and neither do most
- Who can do this work at all is narrowing. Agents make that worse
- Real work is now possible on small open models
